## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Sekhiya 57 (*Chattapāṇi*) of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga is a training rule belonging to the Vinaya Piṭaka regarding decorum when teaching the Dhamma. It regulates that a monastic should not teach the Dhamma to someone who is holding a sunshade (or umbrella), except when that person is ill. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

This rule belongs to a widely shared core of monastic discipline found across nearly all early Buddhist Vinaya lineages. Within the Pali Canon, parallels occur in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk57*), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk57*, *pli-tv-bi-pm-sk57*), and the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Cross-tradition parallels survive extensively in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas. DharmaNexus reports 417 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 103 texts, notably sharing standard Vinaya formulaic language with Khandhaka chapters such as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15) and *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), related Sekhiya rules (e.g., Sk 69, Sk 37, Sk 56, Sk 75), several Pācittiya rules (such as Pc 31, Pc 13, and Pc 27), and the *Vinayapiṭake Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text with a Tibetan Vinaya passage in BO_T08_D4106-1 [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
